The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

To help understand the concept of inflation theory in cosmology, imagine a tiny, wrinkled raisin dough ball. In the early universe, all matter was packed into a space smaller than an atom. Inflation theory suggests that this "dough" expanded incredibly fast, like a loaf of bread rising in an oven. Just as the raisins (representing galaxies) move apart from each other not because they are moving through the dough, but because the dough itself is expanding, the universe expanded so rapidly that distant points moved away from each other faster than the speed of light. This rapid expansion smoothed out the universe and set the stage for the structure we see today.
